Beet Yogurt Dip with Pistachio

Served at: Yalda Night

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 45 min

This vibrant Beet Yogurt Dip, known as Borani Laboo in Persian cuisine, is a refreshing and visually stunning addition to any Yalda Night spread. Yalda Night, or Shab-e Yalda, celebrates the winter solstice, the longest night of the year, and is traditionally marked by gathering with loved ones, reading poetry, and enjoying seasonal fruits like pomegranates and watermelon, as well as colorful dishes like this one. The deep red of the beets symbolizes the dawn and the warmth of the sun, making it a perfect dish to welcome the longer days ahead.

Ingredients

  • 3 medium beets (about 1 pound or 450g), trimmed
  • 2 cups (480g) plain full-fat Greek yogurt
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) fresh lemon juice
  • 1 tablespoon (15ml) extra virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
  • 1/4 cup (30g) shelled pistachios, roughly chopped, for garnish
  • 2 tablespoons fresh mint or dill, chopped, for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. Wash the beets thoroughly. Place them in a medium pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30-45 minutes, or until fork-tender. Alternatively, roast beets wrapped in foil at 400°F (200°C) for 45-60 minutes until tender.
  2. Once cooked, drain the beets and let them cool slightly. When cool enough to handle, peel the skin off (it should slip off easily).
  3. Roughly chop the cooked and peeled beets. In a food processor, combine the chopped beets, minced garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
  4. Process until the mixture is smooth, scraping down the sides as needed. You can leave it slightly chunky if you prefer a different texture.
  5. Transfer the beet mixture to a medium bowl. Add the Greek yogurt and gently fold it in until just combined and uniformly pink. Do not overmix.
  6. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice to your preference.
  7. Cover the dip and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and for the dip to chill.
  8. Before serving, transfer the dip to a serving bowl. Drizzle with a little extra olive oil and sprinkle generously with the chopped pistachios and fresh herbs, if using. Serve with pita bread, crackers, or fresh vegetables.

Tips

  • For a deeper, sweeter flavor, roast the beets instead of boiling them. This caramelizes their natural sugars.
  • Adjust the amount of garlic to your liking; for a milder flavor, use just one clove, or for a stronger kick, add a third.
  • This dip can be made a day ahead and stored in the refrigerator. The flavors will deepen overnight, just give it a good stir before serving and add fresh garnishes.
